(Fa'ida)

Likewise, God's giving 'Abd al-'Uzza the kunya (teknonym) Abu Lahab: since his destination was a Fire of blazing flame, this kunya was more fitting and suitable for him, and he was more deserving of it and more apt for it.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ by what the pen ran with in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz).

God Most High said: ﴿His wealth did not avail him, nor what he earned﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: "What he earned: his son."

God Most High said: ﴿He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame, and his wife﴾.

So (imra'atuhu, "his wife") is in the nominative, in coordination (ataf) with the pronoun in (sayaslá, "he will burn").

God Most High said: ﴿And his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾.

He called her "his wife" by the marriage contract that took place in polytheism.

And God Most High said: ﴿And God presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh﴾ [al-Tahrim: 11], and He called her "wife."

Most of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, were born of marriages that took place before Islam, in a state of polytheism, and they are ascribed to their fathers in a lineage about which no one among the people of Islam has any doubt. Moreover, a great multitude embraced Islam in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and he did not command any of them to renew his marriage contract with his wife.

Had the marriages of the disbelievers been void, he would have commanded them to renew their marriages. The Prophet ﷺ used to invoke blessings upon his Companions' fathers, and this is known necessarily from the religion of Islam. The Messenger of God ﷺ also stoned two Jews who had committed adultery; had their marriages been invalid, he would not have stoned them, because an invalid marriage does not make a spouse muhsan (fully protected by marriage).

Also, the Prophet ﷺ commanded whoever embraced Islam while having ten wives to choose four of them and separate from the rest, and he commanded whoever embraced Islam while having two sisters to keep one of them and separate from the other. Had their marriages been invalid, he would not have commanded retaining them in an invalid marriage, nor would he have attached to it any of the rulings of marriage. No imam of Islam has stated explicitly that the marriages of the disbelievers are void, and no one can say that.
